claim.pdf_says:
CLASS-ID. object-class-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] [ IS FINAL ]
    [ INHERITS FROM { object-class-name-2 } ... ]
    [ USING { parameter-name-1 }  ...  ] .

-- with underlining on IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, CLASS-ID, AS, FINAL, INHERITS, USING, END, CLASS, FACTORY, IMPLEMENTS, OBJECT. IS and FROM are printed WITHOUT underlining (verified by cropping/zooming the rendered page at 300 dpi).
claim.markdown_says:
CLASS-ID. object-class-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] [ IS FINAL ]
　[ INHERITS FROM { object-class-name-2 } ... ]
　[ USING { parameter-name-1 } ... ] .

-- all words plain text; no <u> markers and no 'Figure notes' paragraph recording which words are underlined.
claim.why_it_matters: Per the general-format conventions, an underlined reserved word is REQUIRED and a non-underlined reserved word is OPTIONAL and may be omitted. The PDF prints IS and FROM without underlining, so 'CLASS-ID. C-1 FINAL.' and 'INHERITS { object-class-name-2 } ...' are legal. With the underlining dropped, the markdown reads as though IS and FROM were mandatory -- the falsely-restrictive direction. The same loss applies to the factory-definition and instance-definition skeletons on this page.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on all three legs; I attempted to refute it and could not.

(1) PDF GLYPHS, read directly. Rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v288/spec_p288.png at 300 dpi (2550x3300) and cropped the class-definition skeleton to ~2x magnification (crop_class.png, source box x=250..1500, y=570..800). What I see printed: 'CLASS-ID' carries a horizontal rule ending before its period; 'AS' carries a rule; 'IS' has NO rule beneath it -- clean white space; 'FINAL' carries a rule; 'INHERITS' carries a rule; 'FROM' has NO rule beneath it -- clean white space; 'USING' carries a rule. The two unruled words are unambiguous at that magnification, not faint or clipped: the baseline under IS and under FROM is blank while the adjacent AS/FINAL and INHERITS rules are solid and full-width. Separate crops confirm END + CLASS ruled (crop_endclass.png), FACTORY + IMPLEMENTS ruled (crop_factory.png), and the page-level render shows IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, END, FACTORY, OBJECT, IMPLEMENTS all ruled. The claim's inventory of underlined words is accurate.

(2) MARKDOWN, quoted correctly. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 12535-12566 (page-288 anchor at 12530) reproduce all three skeletons as bare plain text. No <u> markup, no bold, no 'Figure notes' paragraph anywhere in the page-288 block. The claim quotes both sources verbatim.

(3) NOT a global formatting convention -- this is a page-specific loss. The transcription has an established, heavily-used mechanism for exactly this: 97 'Figure notes ... underlined in the printed standard' paragraphs across the file. The two IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT pages both carry one. Line 12512 (page 287, program-definition) ends '...Underlined (required) words in the printed figure: IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, PROGRAM-ID, AS, COMMON, INITIAL, RECURSIVE, END, PROGRAM.' Line 12611 (page 289, method-definition) says verbatim '...`OVERRIDE`, `FINAL`, `END`, and `METHOD` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `IS` is not underlined.' -- i.e. the transcription records precisely this IS distinction one page later, and drops it on page 288. So the omission cannot be excused as 'the markdown never carries underlining'.

(4) MEANING IS LOST, in the falsely-restrictive direction. 5.2.5/5.2.6 (md lines 2628, 2641, 5770, 5805): keywords are 'uppercase and underlined ... required'; optional words are 'uppercase and not underlined ... may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics'. A reader of the markdown alone cannot tell IS and FROM are omissible. Decisive corroboration from the standard's OWN sample code, which omits FROM: 'CLASS-ID. CheckingAccount INHERITS Base.' (md 45770), 'CLASS-ID. Account INHERITS Base.' (46001), 'CLASS-ID. CheckingAccount INHERITS Account.' (46047), 'CLASS-ID. AccountCollection INHERITS Base USING X.' (46420), 'CLASS-ID. Employee INHERITS Base.' (46487), 'CLASS-ID. Account INHERITS Base.' (46609). Six occurrences of INHERITS with no FROM. A parser built from the markdown figure as printed would reject all six of the standard's own examples. That is a normative, falsely-restrictive defect.

Refutation attempts that FAILED: the text is not reflowed onto an adjacent line (there is no underline record anywhere on the page); it is not page-break furniture; it is not mere styling, because the underline is normative metalanguage under 5.2.5/5.2.6 and the transcription itself treats it as content elsewhere; the claim does not misquote either source.

ONE OVERSTATEMENT in the claim, corrected below: the closing sentence generalizes the loss to the factory- and instance-definition skeletons. Those DO lose their underline record, but every reserved word in them (IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, FACTORY, IMPLEMENTS, END, OBJECT) is underlined/required in the print, so no required-vs-optional information is actually destroyed there and no falsely-restrictive reading arises. The normative damage on page 288 is confined to IS and FROM in the class-definition skeleton.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, with narrowed scope and an added sibling sweep.

CONFIRMED CORE: On page 288 the printed class-definition skeleton underlines CLASS-ID, AS, FINAL, INHERITS, USING (and IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, END, CLASS) but prints IS and FROM WITHOUT underlining. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 12537-12540 render the skeleton as plain text with no <u> markup and no 'Figure notes' paragraph, so the required/optional distinction carried by the underline is destroyed. Under 5.2.5/5.2.6 (md 2628, 2641, 5770, 5805) a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word that may be omitted with no semantic effect; the markdown therefore reads as though IS and FROM were mandatory. This is falsely restrictive and is contradicted by the standard's own sample code, which writes INHERITS with no FROM in six places (md 45770, 46001, 46047, 46420, 46487, 46609). Legal forms a markdown-derived parser would wrongly reject: 'CLASS-ID. C-1 FINAL.' and 'CLASS-ID. C-1 INHERITS Base.'

SCOPE CORRECTION: the claim's assertion that 'the same loss applies to the factory-definition and instance-definition skeletons on this page' overstates the impact. Those two skeletons also lose their underline record, but every reserved word in them (IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, FACTORY, IMPLEMENTS, END, OBJECT) is underlined/required in the print, so no optional word is misrepresented and no falsely-restrictive reading follows. The normative loss on page 288 is confined to IS and FROM in the class-definition skeleton.

SIBLING DEFECTS FOUND (sweep targets, same root cause):
  - md line 12816-12818, section 11.3.2 CLASS-ID paragraph General format (page 294): repeats the identical figure ('[ IS  FINAL ]', '[ INHERITS FROM ... ]') with no underline record and no Figure notes. Same normative loss, in the paragraph that is the actual syntax authority for CLASS-ID.
  - md line 12583-12586, interface-definition skeleton (page 289): '[ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 } ... ]' with no Figure notes; same FROM loss.

SECONDARY FORMATTING DEFECTS on page 288 (non-normative, but they mark this block as unprocessed relative to its neighbours): the three skeletons are NOT wrapped in ``` code fences, unlike the equivalent skeletons on pages 287 and 289; and md lines 12539-12540 are indented with U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE rather than ordinary spaces.

REMEDY: fence the three page-288 skeletons and add a 'Figure notes (class-definition general format)' paragraph in the established house style, e.g. "`IDENTIFICATION`, `DIVISION`, `CLASS-ID`, `AS`, `FINAL`, `INHERITS`, `USING`, `END`, and `CLASS` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `IS` and `FROM` are **not** underlined -- they are optional words." Add the equivalent note to 11.3.2 and to the page-289 interface-definition skeleton, and replace the U+3000 indents.
